title: Bazira (Barikot Ghundai)
subtitle: Indo-Greek city and Italian excavations at Barikot, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Ancient Bazira (Barikot Ghundai) excavation
edits: The excavation is the OSM archaeological_site outline (historic=archaeological_site, unnamed, about 3,100 m2, 67 by 75 m), about 290 m south-west of the Ancient Bazira node; the landmark point is its centre. That node is the Wikidata point for Barikot and is not used as the dig. No Commons photo is geotagged.

The rooms and streets inside the OSM outline are estimated from Commons photos 01 and 03 (the grid of rooms along streets, the wall colours, the low heights); no plan of the dig is in the sources. Two streets 4 m wide cross the dig; the rooms are 3.5 to 9 m; the walls are 0.7 to 1.3 m thick and about 0.4 to 2.8 m high, higher towards the dig's edge, with gaps and missing pieces.

The excavated floor follows the DEM inside the outline, coloured pale earth from photo 03. An earth bank about 1 to 1.7 m high and 5 m wide is drawn along the outside of the outline to show that the dig lies below the ground round it: the page cannot lower the DEM, and the dig's depth is not measured (estimated).

One stretch of town wall, 50 m long, 3 m thick and about 2.6 to 3.2 m high, with one rectangular bastion about 8 m along and 5.5 m deep, is drawn beside the excavation to show the kind of wall the sources describe (Wikipedia Barikot: a defensive wall with massive rectangular bastions). Its line is not mapped; its height, thickness and placement are estimated.

The trailhead is the OSM Mingora Road node nearest the dig, about 134 m away on the same side of the Swat river channel. The walk is traced over the DEM and does not cross the river (the nearest river is about 317 m away).

sources.use: the Indo-Greek city wall with massive rectangular bastions; the 12 ha and 7 ha areas; the Macedonian siege in autumn 327 BC; the Italian excavations since 1984; the abandonment by the end of the 3rd century AD
